title: Integrating Inductive Biases in Transformers via Distillation for Financial Time Series Forecasting

problem.claim: Financial markets exhibit regime shifts and non-stationarity that violate assumptions of stationarity and stable temporal dynamics commonly made by Transformer variants.

gap.claim: Existing approaches do not provide a single inductive bias that dominates across markets or regimes, motivating integration of complementary temporal priors.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that state-of-the-art time-series Transformers often underperform vanilla Transformers on financial tasks, while simpler CNN and RNN architectures can achieve stronger performance with substantially lower complexity.

narrative_sequence.summary: Transformers are widely used for generic time-series forecasting because of their representational capacity and architectural flexibility.
Financial markets violate stationarity and stable-dynamics assumptions through regime shifts and non-stationarity.
On financial tasks, complex time-series Transformers may underperform vanilla Transformers and simpler CNN or RNN architectures.
Because no single inductive bias dominates across markets or regimes, robust forecasting may require complementary temporal priors.

source_observation.claim: No single inductive bias dominates across markets or regimes.

interpretation.claim: Forecasting methods should account for variation in market conditions rather than rely on one universally preferred temporal prior.

application.claim: Evaluate or combine multiple inductive biases across markets and regimes.

exception.claim: A particular inductive bias may still perform well in some individual markets or regimes.

unknowns: The abstract units do not specify the proposed distillation method.
The abstract units do not report datasets, metrics, quantitative results, or experimental settings.
The abstract units do not identify how complementary inductive biases are integrated.
